title: Surjective degree-zero derived residue-fibre map
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], and $s\in X$ with residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The degree-zero fibre map is surjective if the canonical map $H^0(K)_s\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,s}}\kappa(s)\to H^0(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s))$ is surjective. Precisely: there is a K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] of $\mathcal O_X$-modules whose image in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is isomorphic to $K$ such that, for its stalk complex $C=P_s$ of $\mathcal O_{X,s}$-modules [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], the cohomology base-change map $c^0_C:\kappa(s)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,s}}H^0(C)\to H^0(\kappa(s)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,s}}C)$ (the map $c^i_K$ of def-pc-module-cohomology-base-change, for $\mathcal O_{X,s}\to\kappa(s)$) is surjective. Exactness of stalks identifies $H^0(C)$ with $H^0(K)_s$, and since $C$ is K-flat, $\kappa(s)\otimes C$ computes $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\kappa(s)$ at $s$; the condition does not depend on the choice of $P$.
